title: getMyTasks merges 8 internal MongoDB sources and 3 microservice fan-outs into one unified list
description: tasks.service.js getMyTasks(): 8 internal sources run via Promise.all (AuditScopeItem, AuditNonConformance, WorkflowEntry-evidence, WorkflowEntry-policy, EvidenceRequest, Finding, ManagementReview, ContinuousImprovement) plus a 9th (AuditAssurance lead/secondary auditor). 3 microservices (vendor-service, risk-management-service, trust-vault-service) are fanned out via Promise.allSettled to GET /internal/tasks.
preconditions: A test user has at least one open item in every one of the 9 internal entity types and in all 3 microservices
steps: Seed one open task per entity type for the test user across all data sources
expectedResult: The response's data.tasks array contains one entry per seeded item (order aside), each shaped as a UnifiedTask with sourceModule correctly set to one of: audit, evidence, policy, cloud-posture, management-review, continuous-improvement, vendor, risk, trust-vault. data.total equals the seeded count.

title: GET /api/tasks returns 200 with _partial=['risk'] when only risk-management-service is unreachable
description: The 3 microservice calls use Promise.allSettled, not Promise.all, so one rejected promise never fails the other two or the internal sources. logServiceFailure logs err.code (network-level, e.g. ECONNREFUSED) vs err.response.status (HTTP-level) distinctly.
preconditions: risk-management-service is stopped or RISK_SERVICE_URL points to an unreachable host
vendor-service and trust-vault-service are healthy and reachable
steps: Call GET /api/tasks for a user with open tasks in vendor, trust-vault, and at least one internal source
expectedResult: Response is 200 (not 500). data.tasks includes vendor/trust-vault/internal tasks but no risk tasks. data._partial equals ['risk'] exactly (not the other two services).

title: GET /api/tasks still returns 200 with internal-only tasks when all 3 microservices are unreachable simultaneously
preconditions: vendor-service, risk-management-service, and trust-vault-service are all stopped or timing out
steps: Call GET /api/tasks for a user with open internal-module tasks only
expectedResult: Response is 200. data._partial contains all three: 'vendor', 'risk', 'trust-vault' (order matches the Promise.allSettled array order). data.tasks contains only the internal-source tasks — the endpoint never hard-fails just because every fan-out call timed out (5000ms axios timeout on each).

title: WorkflowEntry evidence/policy tasks are excluded when the underlying Evidence/Policy document belongs to a different organization
description: Regression guard for TK-009 (fixed): WorkflowEntry has no organizationId field of its own, so fetchWorkflowEntries() aggregates by entityType + assignedTo first, then POST-filters the resulting entityIds against the Evidence or Policy collection (whichever WORKFLOW_ENTITY_MODEL maps to) with organizationId: orgId, keeping only entityIds present in that org-scoped set.
preconditions: User U belongs to Org A
A WorkflowEntry assigns U to review an Evidence document that actually belongs to Org B (simulating a stale/cross-tenant assignment)
A second WorkflowEntry assigns U to review an Evidence document that genuinely belongs to Org A
steps: Call GET /api/tasks as user U with orgId = Org A
expectedResult: Only the Org A evidence review task appears in the response. The Org B evidence review task is silently dropped by the post-filter — it must never surface, confirming no cross-tenant evidence/policy task leak.

title: AuditScopeItem dual-path lookup does not produce a duplicate task when both the direct assignee field and a WorkflowEntry both point to the same item
description: getMyTasks's AuditScopeItem query builds directDocs from the direct assignee field, then computes wfEntityIds by filtering out any entityId already in directIds, so a scope item that has BOTH a direct assignee AND a matching WorkflowEntry is only returned once (from directDocs).
preconditions: An AuditScopeItem has assignee = user U (direct field) AND a WorkflowEntry with entityType='audit_scope_item', metadata.assignedTo = U, status='assigned' pointing at the same scope item
expectedResult: The scope item appears exactly once in data.tasks, not twice.

title: sourceModule + priority + search + assignmentType filters compose correctly (AND semantics)
preconditions: User has: an audit task priority=high assignmentType=owner matching search term 'ISO'; a risk task priority=high assignmentType=owner NOT matching the search term; an audit task priority=low assignmentType=owner matching the search term
expectedResult: Only the single task satisfying all four predicates simultaneously (audit module AND priority=high AND title contains 'iso' case-insensitively AND assignmentType=owner) is returned; the other two tasks (wrong module, wrong priority/no match) are excluded.

title: dueBefore filter includes tasks due on/before the given ISO date and excludes tasks with no dueDate
description: tasks.service.js: `if (dueBefore) filtered = filtered.filter(t => t.dueDate && new Date(t.dueDate).getTime() <= beforeTs)` — note the `t.dueDate &&` guard means a task with no dueDate at all (e.g. any EvidenceRequest task, which always has dueDate=undefined per normaliseEvidenceRequest) can never match a dueBefore filter, however lenient.
preconditions: Task C (an EvidenceRequest task): dueDate = undefined
expectedResult: Only Task A is returned. Task B is excluded (due after the cutoff). Task C is excluded regardless of the cutoff value because it has no dueDate to compare.

title: GET /api/tasks/tab-counts runs owner and review queries in parallel and de-duplicates _partial across both
description: tasks.routes.js: tab-counts issues two independent getMyTasks calls (assignmentType='owner' and 'review') via Promise.allSettled, and merges each result's _partial array through a Set so a microservice outage that affects both calls (it always will, since it's the same downstream dependency) is reported once, not twice, in the combined _partial.
preconditions: The user has both owner and review tasks
expectedResult: Response 200. data.owner.total and data.review.total each reflect only non-vendor tasks (or whatever internal counts remain). data._partial equals ['vendor'] — a single entry, not ['vendor','vendor'] — even though both the owner and review sub-calls independently failed to reach vendor-service.
